title: Neighborhood boys bands, block parties and High School of Commerce bands
summary: He moves uptown, joins the Dover brothers' band, plays block parties and dances, and plays in school bands.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, that was downtown. We slowly moved uptown. This is Manhattten, and I became acquainted with some older fellows, and a boys band was two young fellows. Willie and Lewis Dover, had a band. And I heard of it, and they had heard of me. So we got together. It was a nice little band, young fellows, very young. And we rehearsed together very religiously and all that kind of - we got work. At that time there wasn't very many people in New York, no cars and anything, and
they used to have a lot of block parties. We played for block parties at the end of the week, and my little extra money came in handy, to the family.
So I kept on with them, and from one little band to another, I made progress.
What sort of music were you playing?
Just the ordinary music at that time, like, popular music, mostly. And it was strictly jazz, because we weren't reading much. Although I had been taught to read.
Well, from then on, I joined another little band, and we started to play for little dances. Then I was reading music then. That was really nice, all right.

Well, war came in, and I was playing then, and working and playing and working and playing on the weekends, got a little job. I was still in school. Well, at school, I went to the High School of Commerce. They had an assembly band, orchestra, that is, then they had a band for the football and the baseball games, High School of Commerce, 66th Street off Broadway. They tore it down now, but they had a place there.
